I verified the fix with 4 test cases covering:

| Test | What it checks | Result |
|------|---------------|--------|
| `TestSumFirstN_Bug` | Buggy version panics with index out of range when `n == len(s)` | ✅ PASS |
| `TestSumFirstN_Fixed` | Fixed version returns correct sums for `n = 0, 1, 2, 3` | ✅ PASS |
| `TestSumFirstN_EdgeCases` | Empty slice (`nil`), single element, zero-length request | ✅ PASS |
| `TestSumFirstN_Robust` | Clamped version handles `n > len(s)` gracefully | ✅ PASS |

All tests pass under both normal and `-race` detector conditions.

```
=== RUN   TestSumFirstN_Bug          --- PASS
=== RUN   TestSumFirstN_Fixed        --- PASS
=== RUN   TestSumFirstN_EdgeCases    --- PASS
=== RUN   TestSumFirstN_Robust       --- PASS
PASS  ok  offbyone/offbyone         0.002s
```

**Edge cases tested:**
- `n == len(s)` (the classic off-by-one boundary)
- `n == 0` (empty iteration)
- `n == 1` (single element)
- `n > len(s)` (clamping handled by robust version)
- `nil` slice with `n == 0`
- All slices of length 3
